verdicts.title: get_jit_options accepts any valid JSON, not just a JSON object
verdicts.reasoning: configurations.py lines 12-14 show `as_json = json.loads(as_str); return as_json` with the only guard being `except json.JSONDecodeError`. No `isinstance(as_json, dict)` check exists. The deciding line is line 14: `return as_json` — any JSON value (null, bool, int, list, string) is returned verbatim. Confirmed downstream: work.py line 62 uses `@njit(**jit_options)`, which will raise `TypeError: argument after ** must be a mapping` at import time if jit_options is not a dict. The evidence quote is accurate and the reasoning holds. Severity low is appropriate: only triggered by explicit misconfiguration of the env var.
